                [32m'- A recurring schedule for that worker, plus an endpoint that enqueues it on demand.\n'[39m +

It must also work when re-run later on an already-populated database without destroying stored data.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Server (HTTP API) port: `3001`. Web client port: `3000`.\n'[39m +

                [32m'  "metric": string,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "value": number,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "recordedAt": string\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`recordedAt` is an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Every request must carry an `Idempotency-Key` request header. Responses:\n'[39m +

                [32m'- Any later request reusing an already-seen `Idempotency-Key`: status `200` with body `{"id": number, "duplicate": true}` where `id` is the identifier returned by the first request, and no additional sample is stored.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Status `400` with body `{"error": string}` when the `Idempotency-Key` header is missing or empty, when `metric` is not a registered metric, when `value` is missing or is not a finite number, or when `recordedAt` is missing or is not a parsable ISO-8601 timestamp. Rejected requests must not store anything.\n'[39m +
                [32m"- Any `id` or `ingestedAt` field supplied in the request body is untrusted and must never be used as the stored sample's identifier or ingestion timestamp.\n"[39m +
                [32m'- Concurrency invariant: when N requests carrying the same `Idempotency-Key` and the same body are issued simultaneously, exactly one of them returns `201`, all others return `200`, all of them return the same `id`, and exactly one sample ends up stored.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`POST /api/rollup` — enqueue one rollup run. It must return status `202` with body `{"jobId": string, "jobName": "rollupMetrics"}` immediately, without waiting for the rollup to finish. The enqueued work item must carry the argument `{"reason": "manual"}`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"`GET /api/dashboard` — status `200` with a JSON array holding exactly one object per registered metric, ordered by `metric` ascending, each object having exactly the keys `metric`, `count`, `p95`, `avg`, `delta` and `updatedAt`. The returned numbers must be exactly the values persisted by the most recent rollup of that metric; ingesting samples must never change this endpoint's output until a rollup has run. `updatedAt` is the UTC instant at which the rollup persisted that metric's result, formatted as an ISO-8601 string ending in `Z`. For a metric that has never been rolled up, return `count` `0` and `null` for `p95`, `avg`, `delta` and `updatedAt`.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Rollup semantics\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"One rollup run processes every registered metric. For a metric with at least one stored sample, let `T` be the greatest `recordedAt` among that metric's stored samples, and define:\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- current window: samples with `T - 3600s < recordedAt <= T`\n'[39m +
                [32m'- previous window: samples with `T - 7200s < recordedAt <= T - 3600s`\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'and persist:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `count`: the number of samples in the current window.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `avg`: the arithmetic mean of the current-window values, rounded to 3 decimal places, half away from zero.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `p95`: the nearest-rank 95th percentile of the current-window values, i.e. sort the current-window values ascending and take the value whose 1-based position is `ceil(0.95 * count)`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `delta`: `p95(current window) - p95(previous window)`, rounded to 3 decimal places, half away from zero, or `null` when the previous window contains no samples.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'For a registered metric with no stored samples at all, persist `count` `0` and `null` for `p95`, `avg` and `delta`. Every processed metric gets a fresh persisted timestamp on every run. Rollups must never delete or mutate raw samples.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Background processing\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The rollup work item is queued under the exact name `rollupMetrics`, so a work item with that name enqueued by any producer that talks to the app\'s queue — including one enqueued directly in the database by an external process while the app is running — must be picked up and executed by the running app. In addition, `rollupMetrics` must be registered as a recurring job with the cron expression `23 3 * * *` and the argument `{"reason": "cron"}`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Dashboard page (port 3000)\n'[39m +

            [32m'- If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'  - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)\n'[39m +
            [32m"- You shall avoid use the markdown code block syntax (backtick, '`') in your command, as it will be interpreted as a command substitution.\n"[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m' * We expect this to be called once per job name. If called multiple times with the same name and different\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * functions, we will override the previous calls.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export function registerJob<\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Input extends JSONObject,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Output extends JSONValue | void,\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  jobFn: JobFn<Input, Output, Entities>,\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  // NOTE(shayne): We are not awaiting `pgBossStarted` here since we need to return an instance to the job\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // template, or else the NodeJS module bootstrapping process will block and fail as it would then depend\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // on a runtime resolution of the promise in `startServer()`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // Since `pgBossStarted` will resolve in the future, it may appear possible to send pg-boss\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // a job before we actually have registered the handler via `boss.work()`. However, even if NodeJS does\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // not execute this callback before any job `submit()` calls, this is not a problem since pg-boss allows you\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // to submit jobs even if there are no workers registered.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  // Once they are registered, they will just start on the first job in their queue.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  pgBossStarted.then(async (boss) => {\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    await boss.offWork(job.jobName)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // This tells pg-boss to run given worker function when job with that name is submitted.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // Ref: https://github.com/timgit/pg-boss/blob/master/docs/readme.md#work\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    await boss.work<Input, Output>(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      job.jobName,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      pgBossCallbackWrapper<Input, Output, Entities>(jobFn, job.entities)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    // If a job schedule is provided, we should schedule the recurring job.\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    // If the schedule name already exists, it's updated to the provided cron expression, arguments, and options.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    // Ref: https://github.com/timgit/pg-boss/blob/master/docs/readme.md#scheduling\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    if (job.jobSchedule) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      const options: PgBoss.ScheduleOptions = {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ...job.defaultJobOptions,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ...job.jobSchedule.options,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      await boss.schedule(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        job.jobName,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        job.jobSchedule.cron,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        job.jobSchedule.args,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        options\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +

                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * This is an interface repesenting a job that can be submitted to pg-boss.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * It is not yet submitted until the caller invokes `submit()` on an instance.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * The caller can make as many calls to `submit()` as they wish.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export class PgBossJob<\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Input extends JSONObject,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Output extends JSONValue | void,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Entities extends Partial<PrismaDelegate>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> extends Job {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  public readonly defaultJobOptions: Parameters<PgBoss['send']>[2]\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  public readonly startAfter: number | string | Date | undefined\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  public readonly entities: Entities\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  public readonly jobSchedule: JobSchedule | null\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  constructor(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    jobName: string,\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    defaultJobOptions: Parameters<PgBoss['send']>[2],\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    entities: Entities,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    jobSchedule: JobSchedule | null,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    startAfter?: number | string | Date\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    super(jobName, PG_BOSS_EXECUTOR_NAME)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.defaultJobOptions = defaultJobOptions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.entities = entities\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.jobSchedule = jobSchedule\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.startAfter = startAfter\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  delay(startAfter: number | string | Date) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return new PgBossJob<Input, Output, Entities>(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      this.jobName,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      this.defaultJobOptions,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      this.entities,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      this.jobSchedule,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      startAfter\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  async submit(jobArgs: Input, jobOptions: Parameters<PgBoss['send']>[2] = {}) {\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    const boss = await pgBossStarted\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    const jobId = await (boss.send as any)(this.jobName, jobArgs, {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...this.defaultJobOptions,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...(this.startAfter && { startAfter: this.startAfter }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ...jobOptions,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    return new PgBossSubmittedJob<Input, Output, Entities>(boss, this, jobId)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * A pg-boss specific SubmittedJob that adds additional pg-boss functionality.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'class PgBossSubmittedJob<\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Input extends JSONObject,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Output extends JSONValue | void,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Entities extends Partial<PrismaDelegate>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> extends SubmittedJob {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  public readonly pgBoss: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    readonly cancel: () => ReturnType<PgBoss['cancel']>\n"[39m +
                    [32m"    readonly resume: () => ReturnType<PgBoss['resume']>\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    readonly details: () => Promise<PgBossDetails<Input, Output> | null>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  constructor(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    boss: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    job: PgBossJob<Input, Output, Entities>,\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    jobId: SubmittedJob['jobId']\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  ) {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    super(job, jobId)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    this.pgBoss = {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      cancel: () => boss.cancel(jobId),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      resume: () => boss.resume(jobId),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      // Coarcing here since pg-boss typings are not precise enough.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      details: () =>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        boss.getJobById(jobId) as Promise<PgBossDetails<Input, Output> | null>,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'/**\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * Wraps the normal pg-boss callback function to inject entities, as well as extract\n'[39m +
                    [32m' * the `data` property so the arguments passed into the job are the exact same as those received.\n'[39m +
                    [32m' */\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function pgBossCallbackWrapper<\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Input extends JSONObject,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  Output extends JSONValue | void,\n'[39m +
